pr_body:
Might help fix #779

This PR contains a proposal of how MTP devices like android phones could be accessed by Files UWP.

What works:
* Navigation inside the MTP device
* Pasting/Deleting/Renaming inside the MTP device
* Creating new ~files~ folders inside the MTP device.
Files can only be copied to, explorer does the same
* Opening files inside the MTP device

@duke7553 what do you think?
pr_comments: @gave92 I'm impressed by the amount of work you put into this, and will look forward to learning more about this change tomorrow

**Description of code changes**

The main issue when accessing MTP devices is that windows does not map them to normal drives. Files inside such devices will not have a filesystem "path", which results in the impossibility of using functions such as `StorageFolder.GetFolderFromPathAsync()` and `FindFirstFileExFromApp`.

The only way (I found) to get the contents of a folder is querying the StorageFolder with the `folder.GetFilesAsync()`/`folder.GetFoldersAsync()` methods.
Note: getting the parent of a StorageItem *also* doesn't work (`storageItem.GetParentAsync()` returns null)

To get a storage folder from a path:
- I split the given path into components (the same way it's done for NavigationToolbar)
- For each path component, starting from the drive's Root folder (or the ItemViewModel `CurrentStorageFolder`), I drill down calling folder.GetFolderAsync(component) until I get a reference to the storage item I'm interested in.

This is done in [StorageFileExtensions.GetFolderFromPathAsync](https://github.com/files-community/files-uwp/pull/926/files#diff-195392dca6fb4800c7390cbeb8445ab3R95). This behaves the same as `StorageFolder.GetFolderFromPathAsync` unless we are in a removable drive (where the Root property is not null).
This method returns an object that contains the retrieved StorageFolder and a `Path` that in case of removable drives will be a "virtual" path (= "device_name\folder1_name\folder_2_name...")

Most of the other code changes are simply replacing calls to `StorageFolder.GetFolderFromPathAsync` with `ItemViewModel.GetFolderFromPathAsync`

Pros:
- no changes for normal drives
- done in UWP (I discarded the idea of doing this in the fulltrust process like the recycle bin)

issue_context.title: App crashes when accessing android device's drive
issue_context.body:
**Describe the bug**
App crashes whenever I try to access the drive of my android phone

**To Reproduce**
Steps to reproduce the behavior:
1. Plug-in phone
2. Click on phone under drive section
3. App crashes

**Expected behavior**
Root folder of the phone should be displayed

**Desktop**
 - OS Version: [e.g. Windows 10 1909 18363.778]
 - App version: [v0.8.0.0]

**Additional context**
App even crashes even when trying to copy items from my phone to the my PC's local drive (C:).
comments:
Thank you for reporting this. I found out that this is a larger issue than I originally thought, as we have no way of enumerating the storage items from a phone's internal storage unless it has a path returned on the system. (Which it probably doesn't)

Hopefully, I can work with someone more talented than myself in this area soon.
My initial thought is that we need to build a new way to access devices like this without being so dependent on their root path because those do not exist.
